These interact through layered checks: CSP prevents unauthorized script execution, session tokens validate identity, and TLS secures transport. Failure in any layer introduces cascading risks—CSP bypasses may allow XSS, invalid sessions trigger re-authentication, and TLS misconfigurations expose data. The interplay reflects a dualistic logic: defensive mechanisms (CSP, TLS) protect against external threats while session management defends internal consistency. Each primitive operates under distinct but overlapping assumptions about trust domains and temporal validity, forming a robust yet fragile system prone to configuration drift.
